cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the saints in Ephesus, and he's a prisoner (Ephesians 1:1; 3:1). He's just explained a mystery: through the gospel, the Gentiles are fellow heirs (Ephesians 3:6). Now he gets back to what he started to say, and he turns to the Father.

cards.question: Paul turns to the Father to pray. How does he come before Him?

cards.text: Paul calls Him the Father from whom every family in heaven and on earth derives its name. Friend, the first thing I asked the angel who called me out of that drawer was to keep my name, so this line gets me right in the apron.
Remember, Paul's a prisoner, and he tells them his sufferings for them are their glory (Ephesians 3:1, 13). If I were the prisoner, I'd be praying about MY situation, but Paul prays for THEM.

cards.question: Paul is praying for the saints in Ephesus. What's the first thing he asks the Father to do for them?

cards.text: Paul says this strength comes out of the riches of His glory. And the power? It comes through His Spirit.

cards.question: Paul asks God to strengthen these believers in their inner being.
Paul wants these believers strong inside so that something can happen. What is it?

answers.text: Christ may dwell in their hearts
They may earn a great reward

cards.text: Then Paul paints a picture: these believers, rooted and grounded in love. And he says they will have power to grasp something BIG.

cards.question: Paul says these believers will have power to grasp something big. He pictures each of them grasping it all alone.
Paul says they'll comprehend the length and width and height and depth of Christ's ___.
Paul wants them to know the love of Christ, a love that surpasses knowledge. What does he mean?

answers.text: It's bigger than our minds can hold
It's only for the very wise
It fades once you learn it

cards.text: Then Paul prays they'd be filled with all the fullness of God. Friend, I fill cookie boxes for a LIVING, and if I ever tried to fit ALL of anything into one, that box would need to go lie down somewhere.
Paul's done asking. Now he turns to praise, and he talks about what God is able to do.

cards.question: Paul is praising God now. Compared to all we ask or imagine, how much is God able to do?
Paul says God is able to do immeasurably more, according to His power that is at work ___ us.
Paul closes with "to Him be the glory in the church and in Christ Jesus," and he means only for his own generation.

cards.text: Forever and ever, and Paul seals it with one word: Amen. Paul just prayed the biggest prayer I've ever heard, and friend, I've got goosebumps under this apron.
